name: Digitalisation of judicial cooperation Regulation
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: impact assessment forecasts; no monitoring data or independent studies found
summary: This regulation moves communication between courts and authorities in cross-border cases onto secure digital channels and lets people and firms file claims online and join hearings by video. The Commission forecast savings of about EUR 25 million a year in postage and paper and shorter proceedings. Its obligations are still being phased in, and no data or studies on its effects have been published yet.

indicators.indicator: Number of electronic exchanges via the decentralised IT system, against a baseline of traditional exchanges in a control group of authorities
indicators.target_or_baseline: Monitored annually for at least 5 years from start of digital exchanges
indicators.evidence: No published data found; obligations phase in from 2025 onwards as implementing acts and IT systems are rolled out.

indicators.indicator: Number of electronic claims and submissions by citizens and businesses (e.g. European Small Claims) via the European electronic access point
indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline: paper submissions in control group

indicators.indicator: Yearly savings of about EUR 25.6m in postage and paper (EUR 4.5m for individuals and firms); procedures shortened by ~15.4m days in total per year
One-off IT cost EUR 18.7m over 5 years; recurrent EUR 8.1m/yr at EU-27 level

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals on the digitalisation of judicial cooperation and access to justice in cross-border civil, commercial and criminal matters (executive summary SWD(2021) 393), SWD(2021) 392
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals on the digitalisation of judicial cooperation and access to justice in cross-border civil, commercial and criminal matters (executive summary SWD(2021) 393)
literature.outcomes: administrative costs; case duration; access to justice
literature.headline: Yearly savings EUR 25.59m in postage and paper at EU level (EUR 4.49m for individuals and legal entities); total case duration cut by ~15.4m days a year; one-off IT cost EUR 18.7m over 5 years; recurrent EUR 8.1m/yr; videoconferencing emits 7% of the carbon of physical meetings
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected that moving cross-border court paperwork online would save about EUR 25 million a year in postage and paper and shorten proceedings.

literature.authors: Zoi Kolitsi (AUTH), Mathias Maurer (Austrian Federal Ministry of Justice) and SimpliVi partners
literature.title: SimpliVi Analysis & Design Consolidation (v1.1)
literature.method: qualitative field study: study visits, interviews and questionnaires with judges, court staff, ministries, lawyers and IT staff in 14 EU Member States plus Brazil, Canada and Norway (2023-2025)
literature.outcomes: use of videoconferencing in court hearings, barriers to cross-border videoconferencing, reported efficiency effects
literature.headline: Field research in 14 Member States finds rules on remote hearings still differ widely, and that cross-border videoconferencing is held back by missing contact points, incompatible proprietary systems and legal differences; reported benefits include fewer prisoner transports and faster case closure.
literature.summary_plain: An EU-funded project visited courts across Europe to see how video hearings work, as the new EU digital justice rules start to require them. It found big differences between countries and technical and legal hurdles for hearings across borders.
literature.period_geography: 2023-2025; 14 EU Member States plus Brazil, Canada, Norway
literature.quality: Qualitative baseline mostly before the Regulation's videoconference provisions apply; no quantified outcomes; consortium includes justice ministries.
literature.interested_party: Consortium includes national justice ministries; EU-funded
literature.citation: Zoi Kolitsi (AUTH), Mathias Maurer (Austrian Federal Ministry of Justice) and SimpliVi partners (2025), SimpliVi Analysis & Design Consolidation (v1.1), SimpliVi project (EU Justice Programme), July 2025
